one_liner: Tiny multi-threaded io_uring HTTP/1.1 static-file server in C; edges nginx 1-16% on a 102-byte file, loses on larger files.
what_it_does: Hinsightd MT is a standalone HTTP/1.1 web server: the multi-threaded 0.10 branch of hinsightd. It serves static files with HTTPS/SNI, single-range requests, 304/ETag handling, on-the-fly deflate/gzip and access logs, and has had a basic reverse proxy since April 2024. You configure it with command-line flags or an ini file that uses the same directives (not nginx.conf), and a live console prompt accepts directives while it runs. The build also installs a libhin library and headers, but no library API is documented.
how_it_is_fast: Each worker thread (one per core by default) owns a thread-local io_uring ring created with IORING_SETUP_SINGLE_ISSUER | IORING_SETUP_COOP_TASKRUN. Each thread keeps one accept SQE outstanding on the shared listening socket and then handles that whole connection itself, so little is locked. Submissions are batched: one io_uring_submit per loop pass, and up to 64 CQEs reaped per wait. File open, read, send and close are all asynchronous io_uring operations. Bodies smaller than the ~8 KB buffer are condensed with the headers, and TCP_CORK is set only for larger bodies. That suits the connect-request-close pattern of the tiny-file test. There is no sendfile or splice: file data is read into user-space buffers and then sent, which is why it falls behind nginx on the 89.7 kB file.
when_to_use: Serving tiny static files (a few hundred bytes) to many short-lived connections on a recent Linux kernel. The author's test puts it 7-16% ahead of nginx at 50-250 concurrent ab clients.

Studying or borrowing a compact per-thread io_uring accept/read/send loop in plain C. The core netcode is a few hundred lines per file, the project page says the binary is under 200 KB, and the licence is permissive (BSD-3-Clause text, readme says MIT).
Hobby or dev-box static hosting where one small binary with HTTPS, range and 304 support is enough and pre-1.0 software is acceptable.
A/B experiments of io_uring against epoll in the same server: --force_epoll switches the backend (the author says the epoll path is slower and not very well tested).
when_not_to_use: Files larger than a few KB. It has no sendfile, and on the 89.7 kB jquery.js it reached only 0.68-0.82x nginx's req/s, even with sendfile turned off in nginx to match.
CPU-bound dynamic compression: gzip of jquery.js ran at about 0.75x nginx (727 vs 973 req/s at -c 50), and compression is fixed at zlib level 9.
High concurrency: the tiny-file lead falls to about 1% at c=500-1000. That is within the noise of a best-of-N test with client and server on one machine.

Internet-facing production. The README warns that denial-of-service bugs are 'still likely present', and the 2024 changelog fixes several use-after-free bugs. Keepalive to reverse-proxy backends is marked 'bugged'. There is no FastCGI, no HTTP/2 and no multi-range support.
Non-Linux hosts, and container runtimes that block io_uring syscalls (the README says podman needs --security-opt seccomp=unconfined).

integration.form: Standalone server binary (hinsightd) built from source with CMake/Ninja. The build also produces and installs an undocumented libhin library with headers. This branch has no distro packages; a Dockerfile is provided.
integration.dependencies: liburing, zlib, pthreads, glibc or musl; OpenSSL or LibreSSL (on by default, can be turned off); libsystemd optional (off by default); CMake to build (the README uses Ninja).
integration.min_toolchain: Any C compiler with GNU extensions (__thread, _GNU_SOURCE). CMakeLists.txt declares CMake 3.17 but calls cmake_path unconditionally, and cmake_path needs CMake 3.20. The README says Linux >= 5.6, but the ring is created with IORING_SETUP_SINGLE_ISSUER (Linux 6.0+) and COOP_TASKRUN (5.19+). On older kernels ring setup fails and the server falls back to epoll.
integration.platforms: Linux only (io_uring with an epoll fallback, statx, signalfd); glibc and musl. CPU architectures: not documented.
integration.thread_safety: Inside the server: one event loop and io_uring ring per thread in thread-local storage, each client stays on the thread that accepted it, and shared server, vhost and file-cache state uses locks and atomic helpers. libhin has no documented thread-safety contract.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it replaces nginx only for plain static-file serving (plus a basic reverse proxy since April 2024). It has its own CLI/ini config with no nginx.conf compatibility, and lacks FastCGI, HTTP/2 and sendfile.

gotchas: Kernel mismatch: the README says Linux >= 5.6, but io_uring setup requests IORING_SETUP_SINGLE_ISSUER (6.0+). On older kernels it logs 'io_uring_init failed' and every thread runs the slower, less-tested epoll path, where file reads become blocking pread calls.

The gzip comparison may not be like-for-like. hinsightd hard-codes deflateInit2(Z_BEST_COMPRESSION), while the benchmark's nginx.conf takes gzip_comp_level from a template variable whose value is not shown (nginx's default is 1).

The README lags the code. Its roadmap still says 'readd reverse proxy', but rproxy landed in April 2024 commits (after the benchmarks). It also says MIT while docs/LICENSE.txt holds BSD-3-Clause text.
The benchmarks cover 0.10.1 and 0.10.2 only. Later commits (reverse proxy, an SSL refactor, POST support, a global memory limit) are untagged and unbenchmarked.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: uWebSockets, libhv and io_uring-echo-server (frevib) are libraries or demos you build a server on, and F-Stack keeps nginx itself but moves its network path to DPDK. Pick hinsightd only if you want a ready-made, very small C static-file server whose per-thread io_uring loop you can read end to end. For real static serving, nginx remains the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: These are the author's own ApacheBench runs from February 2024. The page describes them as open-request-close tests, with client and server on one 4-core, non-hyperthreaded machine; the CPU model, compiler and flags are not stated, and each figure is the best of several runs. hinsightd 0.10.2 served a 102-byte file at 124,046 req/s against nginx 1.25.3's 106,615 at -c 50 (about 1.16x), shrinking to about 1.01x at -c 750-1000. With sendfile disabled on every server it reached 0.68-0.82x nginx on the 89.7 kB jquery.js and about 0.75x on dynamic gzip.
status_note: Stale: last commit 2 July 2024 (last tag v0.10.3, Feb 2024), 2 GitLab stars, no issues filed, no packages for this branch. The code is permissively licensed and small enough to read or vendor, but treat it as an unmaintained hobby server.
